SCADA STANDARDS 2.A.1. GENERAL The intent of this section of the document is to provide design and construction standards for implementing selected control and monitoring points in the City water pump houses and sewage lift stations based on the SCADA Feasibility Report and Conceptual Design dated April 2000. This document applies only to Water and Waste SCADA and Alarming Systems that are common among many of the City facilities, and is not intended to serve as a comprehensive tag list for all points within any given facility. It is essential that the designer of any new facility or alterations to a facility exercises sound engineering practice to determine all monitoring, control and SCADA points or alarms that may be required for the facility and its process. See also the City of Whitehorse 1999 Pumphouse and Lift Station Audit report dated November 2000. The common systems within the facilities that are considered in this document include: • Generators • Building Systems • Pumps and all applicable additional instrumentation Throughout this document, input and output points for control and monitoring are referenced with respect to the local PLC in any given facility. 2.A.2 GENERATORS When determining the control and monitoring points for a particular generator at any given site, what must first be determined is whether or not the generator is to be considered an emergency power supply. In general, if a pumping facility is a sewage lift station or is providing water for firefighting purposes or includes valves, controls or other equipment used for firefighting and is supplied by a generator, the generator is to be considered an emergency power supply. If a sewage facility is at risk of overflowing into a water body or compromising human safety the generator is to be considered an emergency power supply. Nonetheless, this should be evaluated and confirmed by the engineer at the time of design Depending on whether or not an emergency power supply system is needed, the points that are to be connected to the station PLC and SCADA system will vary. If the generator is part of an emergency power system, it must conform to the national standard CAN/CSA C282-00 Emergency Power Supply for Buildings. Among the various requirements of this standard is a set of remote monitoring and alarm points that must be included in the system. The expectation is that these remotely annunciated points would be sent to the SCADA system. Page 2.A - 2 November, 2020 CITY OF WHITEHORSE SERVICING STANDARDS MANUAL PART 2 - CONSTRUCTION DESIGN CRITERIA APPENDIX 2.A – SCADA STANDARDS Peak shaving should be considered for all facilities and implemented where beneficial. Should peak shaving be pursued, the logic for determining the requirements for the peak shaving cycle is to be resident in the local PLC rather than the SCADA system. The ability to cause a transfer switch to change to the emergency position, and confirm the transfer, when utility power is available must be included as part of any transfer switch used for peak shaving. See the City of Whitehorse 1999 Pumphouse and Lift Station Audit report dated November 2000, and located in the City of Whitehorse Engineering Services Library[BS1], for additional information on peak shaving. The project was delivered in a phased approach to sequence the work based on the client budget. Back New search Energy efficiency and renewable energy for municipal buildings in Gander Type of initiative FCM Green Municipal Fund Plans, Studies and Pilots (PSP) Sector Energy Project value $223,800 Project Type Feasibility Study Sub Sector Building - New - with Renewable energy Grant amount $104,700 Program type GMF Municipality Town of Gander, NL Status Fully Disbursed Population 11,880 Project timeline 2019 - 2020 Project number 16612 Description The Town Council of the Town of Gander (Gander) wishes to complete a study on the environmental and financial feasibility of implementing energy-efficiency measures with renewable energy to a group of town buildings. The project includes the community centre (which hosts the town’s ice rink), the town hall, the sewage lift station, the water and wastewater treatment plants, the fire hall and the public works depot. Gander has been dealing with issues such as high energy usage, deferred capital expenditures, low thermal comfort and high greenhouse gas emissions. Measures and technologies to be considered in the study include the following: • Light-emitting diode (LED) lighting in all the buildings in the group • Integration of the heating, ventilation and air conditioning (HVAC) system with geothermal heat exchanger, high-efficiency cooling coil, low-emissivity ceiling and central automation system at the community centre • A high-efficiency heat pump system at the water treatment plant • A geothermal system that is vertically integrated with a wind turbine at the wastewater treatment plant • An air-source heat pump at the fire hall and the public works depot The expected environmental benefit is a minimum 30% energy savings in each building included in the study, with some buildings exceeding 50%. Less than 10% of this will come from the wind turbine. A Level 3 American Society of Heating, Refrigeration and Air Conditioning Engineers (ASHRAE) audit will be performed in each building and will include a system-by-system and room-by-room investigation of mechanical and electrical systems. Gander also plans to conduct interviews with town stakeholders to help identify priorities. Preliminary designs, sizing of new equipment and cost estimates are some of the deliverables of this study. This study aligns with Gander’s Five-year Strategic Plan and its Integrated Community Sustainability Plan. This initiative corresponds to Phase 2 of a previous retrofit project completed by Gander in 2012, which was not funded by FCM. Innovative aspect(s): This project is innovative for the size of the town and the number of buildings and measures being considered. The integration of the ice plant and HVAC systems with geothermal storage will be one of only a few similar systems in Newfoundland and Labrador. Lastly, the project’s costs are financed by savings guaranteed under an energy performance contract between Gander and its consultant. Replicability: Ice rinks are very common in communities of all sizes across Canada and usually consume large amounts of energy. If proven feasible and efficient, the integration of the ice plant and HVAC systems with geothermal storage could help other Canadian communities manage the energy consumption and costs of their rinks. Honeywell Contract In 2014 Council entered into an agreement with Honeywell Canada to identify, evaluate, and implement energy saving and carbon reducing measures as part of our commitment to environmental and fiscal responsibility. This initiative has proven to be very successful. Special Meeting of Council April 15, 2020 Page 2 of 3 Improvements in technology and best practices now make it possible to further build on our success. To this end, Honeywell Canada, in conjunction with Town of Gander Management, have evaluated numerous facilities and processes throughout the Town’s operations with the goal to identify opportunities for additional improvement. Council is now prepared to proceed with additional improvements in this, the second phase of our Comprehensive Services Contract with Honeywell Limited. The total cost of this project is $3,949,155 exclusive of HST with 47% funded through special grants and Honeywell fully guaranteeing Council’s share of the overall investment. Work to be completed incudes: • The mechanical retrofit of the Steele Community Center ice plant, • Lighting improvements throughout municipal buildings, • Mechanical System Upgrades in various Town buildings, including a heat pump at the Town Depot • Renewable energy upgrades such as a Passive Solar Wall and Thermal Storage system at the Steele Community Centre, • An evaluation and recommendations on Electrical/Fleet Feasibility Measures, and • A Communications and Awareness Plan Council is very pleased that $1,851,965 the total project is being funded through various grants and agreements with other levels of government and partners, including: • $953,096.80 under the Government of Canada’s Climate Change Challenge Fund (CCCF), • $794,167.91 The Government of NL’s Low Carbon Economy Leadership Fund Agreement, and • $104,700 Federation of Canadian Municipalities Some of the major benefits of the Project include: • A reduction of 231 tons of CO2 greenhouse gas, • Partial mitigation of expected utility price escalation, and • A number of important infrastructure upgrades at the Steele Community Centre. Motion #20-099 Honeywell Contract Moved by Councillor Woodford and seconded by Deputy Mayor Pollett that the Town of Gander approve the amendment to the original Comprehensive Services Contract Between the Town Council of the Town of Gander and Honeywell Limited to include work as described and outlined as “Schedule B-Phase 2020”. In Favour: 7 Opposing: 0 Special Meeting of Council April 15, 2020 Page 3 of 3 Decision: Motion carried. There were inquiries regarding the details of the guarantee provided by Honeywell. The Director Engineering explained that the program is funded through energy savings realized though the upgrades. The Town of Gander finances the project and a 3rd party audit is completed each year of the 10-year contract. If the Town of Gander does not realize enough savings to offset the cost of financing the project, Honeywell Limited will offset the difference. In the event that that there are excess savings realized, the Town of Gander is sole the beneficiary of those savings. The Town of Gander is protected from any risk associated with the project. Thanks to investments by Infrastructure Canada, the terminal has undergone significant upgrades, promising a seamless experience for all travelers. Did you know? This ferry terminal serves as a vital link between Nova Scotia and the United States, offering safe and efficient transportation and playing a crucial role in the local tourism industry. The relocation and upgrade of service provider toll booths streamlines the entry process, ensuring passengers and vehicles alike can embark on their journeys without a hitch. Lighting improvements and the integration of advanced electrical systems, including state-of-the-art CCTV and Public Awareness systems, bolster safety and security measures. Extensive upgrades and repairs to the transfer bridge and pontoon also ensure the safety and integrity of ferry operations, giving travelers peace of mind during their voyage. Asphalt improvements guarantee a smooth transit for both vehicles and pedestrians. This enhancement promises a hassle-free journey for all travelers, contributing to a more seamless overall experience. Strategic upgrades to the Canadian Border Services Agency’s (CBSA) Primary Inspection Line Booths have significantly improved the customs process. Additional modifications to the existing terminal building cater specifically to CBSA's triage and retention requirements, rendering the terminal more functional and accommodating for all passengers. With these revitalizations, the Yarmouth Ferry Terminal not only ensures a safe, efficient, and enjoyable travel experience, but also provides a significant boost to the local tourism industry. Both tourists and residents can rely on this vital link for their travel needs between Nova Scotia and the United States. Quick facts As of September 11, 2023, the Yarmouth Ferry Terminal sold almost 39,000 tickets to passengers who will travel during the 2023 operating season, which runs from May-October. The Yarmouth Ferry Terminal was funded in part by Infrastructure Canada’s New Building Canada Fund (Provincial-Territorial Infrastructure Component – Small Communities Fund – PTIC-SCF) which provides funding for infrastructure projects in communities with populations of 100,000 or less. The PTIC-SCF supports projects that contribute to economic growth, a clean environment and stronger communities. CITY OF ESTEVAN POLICIES AND PROCEDURES MANUAL POLICY # 2024-86 SUBJECT: SURVEILLANCE CAMERA POLICY BACKGROUND City of Estevan is committed to the ongoing protection of the health and safety of employees, customers, and visitors, as well as the protection of properties, both physical and intellectual. In pursuit of this commitment, the City of Estevan has adopted the Policy for Video Surveillance and Accessibility to ensure that appropriate surveillance of company premises is performed, which will help achieve a secure and safe workplace. GOALS The Policy's goal is to guarantee that the correct procedures will be followed for handling, accessing, and viewing video surveillance recordings inside the City of Estevan. The Policy aims to provide for consistent management of the information collected by the video surveillance Programs. GUIDELINES City of Estevan uses video surveillance, recording, and monitoring to monitor a reasonable deterrent for inappropriate criminal activity, overall ensuring a safer, and secure workplace. Notification “Surveillance cameras are in use for the protection of Visitors, Employee and City property (excluding Police Services). The city has a duty to notified public and Employees the presence of Video Surveillance cameras. Notification of Video surveillance signage that is displayed will state: “The property is protected by Video Surveillance. The collection of personal information through the recording of video surveillance image is authorized under section 24 of The Local Authority Freedom of Information and Protection of Privacy Act. For any questions about this surveillance, contact the City Clerk. Safeguard of Video Surveillance Recordings Recording equipment must be located in a controlled access area with only authorized persons having access. The Third-Party services providers who may have access to the recorded information must be bonded and sign a City of Estevan Confidentiality Form (Appendix “A”). Service provider must enter into service agreement with the City to address confidentiality, protection information, as well as access, use disclosure, retention and destruction of video footage. City of Estevan Policies & Procedures Manual Policy # 2024-86 Page 2 Authorized Personnel: The following personnel are approved to access and view video surveillance footage: a) City Manager b) Human Resources c) Privacy Officer Condition for Viewing: Video surveillance footage may only be accessed and viewed under the following conditions: a) Security and safety Investigation: To investigate security breaches, safety incidents, criminal activities, or other incident that pose a threat to the City of Estevan’s property (excluding Police Services), personnel, or public safety. b) Legal requests legislated and or requirements under law enforcement agencies. c) Access to information requests Access to Recorded Video Surveillance Recording: The Privacy Officer, Human Resources or City Manager will review complaints or incidents details to determine whether access to the video recording capturing the incident meets the stated purpose of the Video Surveillance program before granting access as a post investigative tool. Public Safety is addressed with live feed of public areas. Recorded video surveillance footage is stored securely and is typically only reviewed when an event has taken place, or a report or request has been filed that requires the video to be reviewed. To ensure the ongoing privacy of staff and the public at large, the City ensures only authorized personnel are allowed to operate and access video surveillance equipment and review recordings. Individual who are the subject of the information have right to access their own recorded personal information by making the request in writing or submitting an Access to information Request form • They must show the City two pieces of ID (one government issued photo) before the release of the footage. The employee will only indicate on the form or citizen’s letter that the ID was shown, and evidence of their true identity was satisfied. A copy of the ID is not to be retained. • Access may be granted in full or in part depending upon whether any of the exceptions in the Act apply and whether the exempt information can reasonably be severed or blurred from the recordings. If technology provides for blurring of images, that option may be pursued. Otherwise still photos may be provided. Disclosure of recorded video surveillance recordings: Disclosure to a law enforcement agency requires the completed LAFOIP – Law Enforcement Disclosure Request form be submitted to the City before any footage is disclosed (Appendix “C”). Disclosure to government agencies requires the completed Government Institution Disclosure Request form be submitted to the City before any footage is disclosed (Appendix “D”). Use of footage: • Surveillance cameras shall be used for the sole purposes of deterring theft, violence and other criminal activity and ensuring the safety of employees and those accessing our City of Estevan Policies & Procedures Manual Policy # 2024-86 Page 3 facilities. At no time shall the cameras be used to monitor employee productivity or performance. • In the event of a reported or observed incident, the recorded footage may be used to assist in the investigation of the incident and may be turned over to law enforcement or other government personnel, if appropriate. • At no time will persons other than those designated or Human Resources Manager have access to the footage made in the course of surveillance. Personal information contained on the footage shall not be used or disclosed for purposes other than those for which it was collected, except with the consent of the individual or as required by law. • Footage from the surveillance cameras will be stored electronically at the facility as storage space allows for the purposes outlined in this policy. If footage has been used to investigate an incident, that footage will be retained as per the Records Retention and Disposal Bylaw. Access and viewing procedures: a) Authorized personnel must submit a written request to the City Manager, Human Resources Manager, Privacy Officer or designated authority specifying the reason for accessing the footage and the relevant date/time range of the incident. b) The City Manager, Human Resources Manager, or designated authority will review and approve the access request. c) Upon approval, authorized personnel will be provided with secure access to view the requested footage. Access credentials must be kept confidential and not shared with unauthorized individuals. d) All personnel viewing the footage must do so in a controlled and secure environment to prevent unauthorized access or recording. Documentation of all uses, disclosures or accesses of video surveillance recordings: Records documenting all uses, accesses, and releases of video surveillance recordings must be logged to comply with the Act and Video Surveillance Policy. The log should include the following information: • Date and time of access. • Name and job title of the authorized personnel accessing the footage • Reason for accessing the footage • Specific cameras or locations viewed • Duration of the viewing session The log should be retained as per the City of Estevan Records Retention and Disposal Bylaw and made available for audit or review purposes. Non- Disclosure and Data Protection: • Authorized personnel must not disclose or share video surveillance footage with individuals who are not directly involved in the investigation or authorized to access the footage. • All video surveillance footage must be handled in compliance with applicable data protection laws and regulations to safeguard the privacy and rights of individuals captured in the recordings. Data Collection and Security City of Estevan Policies & Procedures Manual Policy # 2024-86 Page 4 City of Estevan securely retains and stores all video surveillance footage data as storage space allows and Records Retention & Disposal Bylaw. Footage and location data may be retained longer where it is required as part of an investigation or for evidence as required by law. Once video surveillance footage and location data are no longer required, they are permanently destroyed or at the very least de- identified. Requests to view surveillance recordings must be made in writing and are at all times subject to approval by authorized personnel. Requests for access are bound by and subject to privacy law and other applicable legislation. If any law enforcement agency requests access to company surveillance data and recordings, the company will act in accordance with the law / LAFOIP/ PICC and provide the materials as is deemed legally necessary. Unauthorized Access or Disclosure: All video surveillance recordings and tracking data remain the property of City of Estevan and may not be reproduced, disseminated, or destroyed for any reason whatsoever without the company’s prior written consent. Only authorized personnel may delete surveillance data and recordings, in line with the requirements of this policy. City of Estevan employees who witness or are made aware of any unauthorized access, disclosure, or breach of this policy, or believe that a potential privacy breach has taken place, must report the incident to authorized personnel and Privacy Officer in the case of Privacy Breach immediately for further action. Any unauthorized access, sharing, or misuse of video surveillance footage will result in disciplinary action as per discipline Policy. Policy Review: This policy will be subject to periodic review to ensure its effectiveness and compliance with changing laws and regulations. Policy Communication: This policy will be communicated to all relevant personnel and stakeholders to ensure awareness and understanding of its provisions. RESPONSIBILITIES The City Clerk or IT will be responsible for reviewing and updating this policy periodic as revision in legislation and Changes to technology.
